To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) cochlear microphoic potentials are of no use in determining hearing threshold, (2) auditory nerve and brainstem neural evoked responses can be used in determining hearing threshold and in locating lesions in the auditory pathway, and (3)cortical evoked responses are useful in locating lesions in higher centers in the auditory pathway.
the auditory nerve and the brain stem responses are the best indicator of hearing threshold.
the auditory nerve and the brain stem evoked responses can be used to evaluate hearing threshold.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an electrophysiological method for the objective evaluation of hearing.

the evaluation of the reliability of the auditory evoked responses in the diagnosis and management of patients with hearing impairment and with the study of the auditory evokd response in the evaluation of the auditory system in normal subjects.

the development and evaluation of the auditory pathway electric response (EP) audiometry, and the results of this study have shown that EP audiometry is a reliable, accurate, objective, quantitative and noninvasive method for the evaluation of hearing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cochlear microphonics are not useful in determining hearing thresholds.

the auditory nerve and the brain stem neural responses are the most reliable indicators of hearing threshold and that all types of evocked responses are indispensable aids for the evaluation of hearing.

the auditory nerve and the brain stem responses are the most reliable indicators for the hearing threshold, and the cortical evoked potentials are the most reliable indicator for the site of lesion in a hearing impaired individual.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the auditory nerve and the brain stem evoked potentials can be used to determine the hearing threshold and the site of lesion in patients with hearing impairment.
the evoked responses can be a very useful aid in the evaluation of auditory function.
the auditory nerve and the brain stem neural responses are the best for determining hearing threshold and for the evaluation of hearing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the auditory nerve and the brain stem responses are the best indicator of hearing threshold.
, the threshold for the auditory nerve and the brain stem neural evoking response is within a few decibel of the behavioral hearing threshold.
the auditory nerve and the brain stem evoked response thresholds are comparable to the behavioural hearing thresholds, and that these two types of responses should be used for hearing assessment.
